# Plan: nested self-referenced cascade delete → every descendant deleted, no error, no dangling refs

Status: DRAFT

Reproduced with a scratch test: collection `selfc` has a multi `rel` field (cascade) pointing at itself, with `a.rel=[p]`, `b.rel=[p,a]`, `a1.rel=[a]`. Deleting `p` returns nil, but `b` survives with `rel=[a]`, which points at the deleted `a`. Cause: `p`'s children are loaded as one batch before `a`'s nested cascade runs, so `b` is handled from stale data.

## Claims

| # | Claim | Kind | Blocks done? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c1 | Deleting a root in a self-referenced cascade tree (single and multi `rel`, 3+ levels, siblings) returns nil and removes every descendant; unrelated records in the collection stay | behavior_change | Yes |
| c2 | A child that references both the deleted root and a sibling that gets cascade-deleted (`b.rel=[p,a]`) is deleted too, not left with a dangling id | behavior_change | Yes |
| c3 | A record that a nested cascade deletes while it is also in the outer batch (two self-rel fields: `a.rel1=p`, `b.rel1=p`, `b.rel2=a`) causes no error and is gone afterwards | behavior_change | Yes |
| c4 | Existing behaviour stays the same: non-cascade refs are unset (not deleted), required non-cascade refs still block the delete, cross-collection cascade and 4000-row batching work as before | no_behavior_change | Yes |

## Checks

| Claim | Type | Check | New? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c1 | Unit | `TestRecordDeleteSelfReferencedCascade` (core/record_model_test.go), parametrized over MaxSelect 1 and 5: delete `p`, expect nil err and only `x` remaining | New |
| c2 | Unit | same test, multi case with `b.rel=[p,a]`: expect `b` deleted | New |
| c3 | Unit | same test, two-field case: expect nil err and only the unrelated record left | New |
| c4 | Unit | existing `TestRecordDelete`, `TestRecordDeleteBatchProcessing` | Existing |

Regression scope: `go test ./core -run 'TestRecordDelete'` · baseline: 2 passed, 0 failed
Skipped: API-level tests (apis/record_crud), since they run the same code path the core tests cover; the full `./core` suite, which is slow in Docker and doesn't touch this code.

Approve, or edit?

The fix is in: deleting a record now removes every self-referenced descendant, without an error and without leaving records behind. The bug came from stale batch data. `deleteRefRecords` (`core/record_model.go`) now reloads each self-referenced child before handling it, and skips it if a nested cascade already deleted it.

The new `TestRecordDeleteSelfReferencedCascade` has 4 cases; only the "child references both the root and a deleted sibling" case failed before the fix, and all 4 pass now. The regression scope (`TestRecordDelete*`) shows no new failures.

Cycles that go across collections (A→B→A) could in theory hit the same stale data. I left those out of scope.

Details are in `.verify/report.md`.
